title: Detect holes puts a bore far wider than the tool into a Bore op, which plunges at its centre and leaves a free core, verified ok

body:
Found while programming a simple 2.5D end-cap plate (user's project) with the CamCraft **v0.19.0** release CLI (macOS arm64), driven headlessly over MCP. Re-checked on upstream main **d00243a5**: **still reproduces, identical hole list and path**.

The user's part (`End Caps-End capSupport Plate.step`, FreeCAD): a plate 101.6 x 177.4 x 10 mm with one Ø74.305 mm through bore and four Ø6 mm through holes.

## What happens

1. `detect_holes` on a Bore op (tool: catalog `EM-0400-2FL`, a 4 mm end mill) lists **5 holes**: the four Ø6 holes **and the Ø74.3 bore** (`"radius": 37.152667, "through": true`). There is no size limit relative to the tool or the op, and no note.
2. Generated as is, the Bore op machines the Ø74.3 bore like a small hole. At each 2 mm level it **plunges the 4 mm end mill at the bore centre**, feeds a full-width straight slot 35.15 mm out to the wall, retracts to clearance, re-plunges at the wall and runs one ring at R35.15. The result is a groove round the wall plus one slot, leaving a **Ø66 mm core disc** in the middle, which breaks free at the last level when nothing under the part holds it. `generate` says `ok`, `verify` says `ok: true` with no findings or warnings, and the program posts.

From the path (main, part bottom at z 4.826; moves 155-163, one level):

```
rapid  (0, 37.9, 40.33) -> (0, 37.9, 16.826)
plunge (0, 37.9, 16.826) -> (0, 37.9, 14.826)        <- centre of the Ø74 bore, into solid
feed   (0, 37.9, 14.826) -> (35.153, 37.9, 14.826)   <- full-width slot to the wall
rapid  up to 40.33, back down to 16.826 at (35.153, 37.9)
plunge -> 14.826 ; three arcs: one ring at R35.153
```

In the user's project the bore was removed from the list by hand (and roughed with a 2D Adaptive instead).

## Minimal repro (MCP)

```
import_model   {"path": "End Caps-End capSupport Plate.step", "name": "part"}
move_model     {"name": "part", "position": [0, 37.9, 4.826]}
add_setup      {"name": "Setup 1"}
set_stock      {"box": {"dx": 110, "dy": 185, "dz": 15.33}}
set_wcs        {"stock_point": {"x": "center", "y": "center", "z": "max"}}
add_tool       {"catalog": "EM-0400-2FL", "name": "EM4"}
add_operation  {"kind": "Bore", "tool": "EM4", "name": "Bore", "source": "part", "params": {"stepdown": 2.0}}
detect_holes   {"name": "Bore"}   -> "holes": 5 (one of radius 37.152667)
generate {} ; verify {}           -> ok, no findings
```

Any plate with one hole much larger than the tool (e.g. a Ø40 bore with a 6 mm tool) shows the same.

## Expected

- Hole detection for a Drill, Bore or Thread op leaves out holes the op's tool cannot make as a hole, and says so: for a Bore op, a hole wider than the size a single helical or circular pass clears without leaving a core (about two tool diameters); for Drill, a hole that is not the drill's size. A note names what was skipped ("Ø74.3 bore skipped: wider than 2 x the 4 mm tool - use a pocket or adaptive"), or the threshold is a visible setting.
- A Bore op given such a hole by hand (edited list) either clears the core (spirals out from the centre helix) or refuses by name. It never plunges into solid at the centre and leaves a free core with an `ok` verdict.

## Done means

- `detect_holes` on the user's plate (or a plate with a Ø40 bore and a 6 mm tool) lists only the holes the op can make, with a note naming each skipped bore and why; pinned by a test.
- A Bore op holding a hole whose ring would leave a core either clears it or refuses at generate with the hole named; pinned by a test.

The through-hole floor rule is #1557.
